entities.blurb: Absorption is a status effect that pads the health bar with extra hearts.
entities.name: Absorption

sections.behaviour: Absorption adds 4 additional [[health]] points per level to the entity, for the player displayed as yellow hearts above the normal health bar. If the entity takes [[damage]] while under this effect, the absorption health points are depleted first, followed by the standard health points. Absorption health cannot be replenished by natural regeneration or other effects and vanishes when the effect ends. Negative absorption levels do not appear to have an immediate effect when applied but give 4 additional health points per level to the entity when the status effect ends.

entities.blurb: Bad Omen is a status effect only obtainable from consuming an ominous bottle. It can transform into Raid Omen in a village to start a raid, or into Trial Omen when seen by a non-ominous trial spawner to start an ominous trial.
entities.name: Bad Omen

sections.behaviour: Bad Omen can be obtained by consuming an [[ominous bottle]], obtained from either killing [[raid captain]]s outside of a raid or from [[vault]]s. Being affected by Bad Omen allows players to initiate [[ominous event]]s. If a player enters a village with Bad Omen, it transforms into [[Raid Omen]], which triggers a [[raid]] after 30 seconds. If the omen level is above 2, an extra wave of raiders will occur after the final wave. Each level after the second will increase the enchantment level of the incoming raiders' equipment, and the resulting [[Hero of the Village]] effect will match the level of the omen, if all raiders have been defeated with villagers still alive. If the player has the Bad Omen effect and goes near a non-ominous [[trial spawner]], it transforms into [[Trial Omen]], which converts all nearby [[trial spawner]]s into [[ominous trial spawner]]s that are significantly harder to deal with and also have better loot. The omen lasts for 15 minutes multiplied by the level of the Bad Omen. Defeating an ominous trial spawner allows the player to obtain [[ominous trial key]]s, which in turn open [[ominous vault]]s that can drop loot of significantly higher quality, including one of two [[Trial Chambers|trial chamber]] exclusive [[smithing template]]s and the [[heavy core]] needed to craft the [[mace]]. Bad Omen is a [[status effect]] and can be removed through all conventional methods, such as drinking [[milk]] or dying. The player can still receive the Bad Omen effect in Peaceful difficulty via [[vault]]s (all pillager captains despawn in Peaceful), but does not transform into [[Raid Omen]] if in a village.

entities.blurb: Blindness is a status effect that impairs a player's vision and prevents sprinting and critical hits. It has no potion, but it can be obtained by consuming suspicious stew made with an azure bluet or open eyeblossom.
entities.name: Blindness

sections.behaviour: Blindness impairs a player's vision by surrounding them with a thick black [[fog]], with only the immediate area around them being visible. With [[Vibrant Visuals]], all directional light sources are disabled, making the scene appear as in a cave. All fog types apart from default air fog still use their colors. The effect also prevents the player from [[sprinting]] or inflicting [[critical hits]]. However, The effect can be removed by drinking [[milk]]. Blindness has no effect on [[mob]]s. This can be observed in [[Survival]] by having a [[fox]] eat suspicious stew made with an azure bluet or open eyeblossom. [[Warden]]s are naturally blind and instead rely on detection via [[vibration]]s, smell and touch. This form of blindness is completely independent from the Blindness effect.

entities.blurb: Conduit Power is an area-of-effect status effect given by active conduits to players touching water or rain. It is a combination of Water Breathing, Haste, and Night Vision.
entities.name: Conduit Power

sections.behaviour: Players under the effect of Conduit Power receive all of the benefits of [[Water Breathing]], [[Night Vision]], and [[Haste]]. This means that their breath meter does not decrease, it gets filled up even underwater, they can sleep in a waterlogged [[bed]], and their mining speed increases. Higher levels of Conduit Power can be obtained only by using commands, in which case Conduit Power X provides the same effect as Haste X, and the other two abilities are unaffected by level. Despite the effects, Conduit Power does not stack with Water Breathing, Night Vision, or Haste. The strongest Haste effect is used, and all timers continue to count down.

entities.blurb: Darkness is a status effect that impairs a player's vision. It is caused by the activation of a naturally-generated sculk shrieker, or by being within detection range of a warden.
entities.name: Darkness

sections.behaviour: Darkness, when applied, dims the player's vision using a thick black [[fog]] similar to [[Blindness]]. After the effect initiates, the fog steadily closes in around the player, diminishing the player's eyesight. The player can only see about 14 blocks away. With [[Vibrant Visuals]], all directional light sources are disabled, making the scene appear as in a cave. All fog types apart from default air fog still use their colors. When the effect wears off, the fog retreats and the player's vision reverts to normal. With the Darkness effect, the screen's brightness slowly cycles every few seconds between complete darkness, and relative visibility where they can see within a distance of roughly 14 blocks., which is normally at 100%; when set to 0%, the player's vicinity does not darken at all, but fog still restricts their vision. Unlike other status effects, Darkness does not cause [[particles]] to appear around the player when it is naturally activated, nor does its icon appear in the player's [[heads-up display]]. This is similar to when an effect is given using the /effect command with the hideParticles argument set to true. However, the particles do appear when hideParticles is set to false, and the effect's icon can be seen when entering the player's [[inventory]].

entities.blurb:
Dolphin's Grace is a status effect that increases an entity's speed while they are in water. It is obtained by sprint-swimming while a dolphin is nearby.
Dolphins grant a similar speed boost in Bedrock Edition, but this version of the mechanic has no name or icon and is not considered to be a standard status effect.
entities.name: Dolphin's Grace

sections.behaviour: Dolphin's Grace causes the player to swim significantly faster and lose speed at a slower rate, but also makes changing directions slower. Dolphin's Grace on its own allows players to travel 9.8 m/s underwater without [[Depth Strider]], making it faster than a [[boat]]. Combining it with Depth Strider, players are able to travel at much higher speeds, adding 8.983 m/s per level. Potentially higher speeds are possible by adding [[soul soil]] underwater and using [[Soul Speed]]-enchanted boots, along with the [[Speed]] status effect.

sources.name: Dolphin
sources.note: The player must sprint-swim within 9 blocks (Euclidean) of a dolphin to achieve this effect with it being replenished if the player continues sprint-swimming within 15 blocks (Euclidean)

entities.blurb: Fire Resistance is a status effect that grants the affected entity complete immunity to all sources of fire damage.
entities.name: Fire Resistance

sections.behaviour: Fire Resistance grants immunity to all kinds of fire damage, including [[fire]], [[blaze fireball]]s, [[fire charge]]s, [[magma block]]s, and [[lava]]. It also negates any bonus fire damage from [[bow]]s enchanted with [[Flame]] and [[sword]]s enchanted with [[Fire Aspect]], but the attacks themselves are unaffected. Fire damage is defined by the game as any [[damage type]] in the minecraft/tags/damage_type/is_fire [[tag]]. Custom damage types defined by [[data packs]] can be added to this tag to allow damage dealt with the damage type through the /damage command to be negated by Fire Resistance. This effect does not work against direct hits/explosions from [[ghast]] fireballs or against melee attacks from a [[blaze]], as neither of these sources are considered to deal fire damage. It does, however, prevent damage from any fire created by a ghast's fireball. Fire Resistance also reduces the [[fog]] effect created due to being submerged under lava. Any [[undead]] mobs that receive Fire Resistance do not take damage from exposure to [[Sun#Effects_on_mobs|sunlight]]. In [[Java Edition|Java Edition]], Fire Resistance does not prevent the affected target from catching fire, but it does prevent any damage that would normally be taken due to being set on fire. This can cause the player (or mob) to start taking damage if the effect expires before said player/mob is able to put themselves out. Fire Resistance allows [[snow golem]]s to survive in hot [[biome]]s.

sources.name: Potion of Fire Resistance
sources.note: [[Witch|Witches]] drink this potion when set on fire or in lava.

entities.blurb: Glowing is a status effect that shows entity positions through blocks.
entities.name: Glowing

sections.behaviour: The Glowing effect causes [[entities]] to glow with an outline that can be seen through [[block]]s and entities. This outline is white by default, but can be set to display other colors if the entity is part of a [[team]] (the color being the color of the team). The outline displays around any holes in a mob's texture or model, though only when that part of the model can be seen all the way through. If multiple entities with glowing are near each other, the outlines merge to prevent overlapping/Z-Fighting. This does not affect mob models as seen in the inventory, of either the player or ridden mobs.

entities.blurb: Health Boost is an unused status effect that increases maximum health of an entity.
entities.name: Health Boost

sections.behaviour: It adds 4 maximum health per level. Unlike [[Absorption]], the added hearts are empty at first, but can be healed through the usual methods (such as natural regeneration and the [[Regeneration]] and [[Instant Health]] effects). Health of any entity is capped at 1024 and extra health provided by Health Boost can't exceed that, so for players, maximum health is reached at Health Boost level 251. Extra hearts of a mounted [[mob]] can be seen while riding it. When the effect ends, any extra health is lost. Losing this extra health causes [[damage tilt]], even if in [[Creative]] or [[Spectator]] mode.

entities.blurb: Hunger is a status effect which causes hunger and saturation to deplete faster than normal.
entities.name: Hunger

sections.behaviour: Hunger increases [[food]] exhaustion by 0.005 × level per game [[tick]] (removes 1 saturation point every (40 ÷ level) seconds). It also turns the hunger bar a yellow-green color. Negative levels decrease food exhaustion, although they do not increase saturation or the hunger bar. The status effect does not decrease hunger level on [[Peaceful]], although it still recolors the hunger bar. Hunger inflicted by eating [[rotten flesh]], [[raw chicken]] or by being attacked by a [[husk]] (if status effect lasts long enough) adds 3.0 to the player's exhaustion level over the course of 30 seconds, draining 3/4 of a saturation point. When a [[Pufferfish (item)|pufferfish]] is eaten, 4.5 exhaustion points are added over the course of 15 seconds, draining 1 and 1/8 (0.125) saturation points.

sections.behaviour: Infested entities have a 10% chance to spawn 1–2 silverfish when hurt. The silverfish spawn at the center of the affected entity's [[bounding box]], and fling out in the direction the entity is facing. The damage source does not necessarily need to reduce the health of the affected entity. For example, a [[snow golem]]'s snowball may trigger a silverfish spawn. The quantity and chance of silverfish spawning are unaffected by the potency level of the potion. Entities with the Infested effect emit gray, silverfish-shaped particles.

When applied using a [[lingering potion]], damage is inflicted every second. As this is magic damage, it can be decreased only via [[Resistance]] and [[Protection]]. Instant Damage has its duration set in game ticks (instead of seconds) with the /effect command.

sections.behaviour: Luck adds the effects level to the [[Attribute#Luck|luck attribute]], which affects the results of [[loot table]]s, with a higher attribute value increasing the amount and quality of results. The number of rolls is increased by the [[Loot table#Pool|pools]] "bonus rolls"-value times this attributes value, rounded down, and the weight of each [[Loot table#Entry|entry]] is increased by its quality times this attributes value, also rounded down. Quality is currently only used by [[fishing]].

entities.blurb: Nausea is an effect that temporarily warps and wobbles the player's vision similarly to a Nether portal. In Java Edition, the "Distortion Effects" setting can reduce the intensity of the wobbling (or stop it completely), substituting it with green-tinted vision.
entities.name: Nausea

sections.behaviour: Nausea causes the [[player]]'s vision to warp and wobble, with the distortion ramping up and down at the start and end of the effect. Although Nausea can be given in the normal range of levels, the level has no impact; it does not affect the distortion. Nausea is affected by the "Distortion Effects"/"Screen distortion" option under the [[video settings]]/[[Settings#Accessibility|accessibility settings]]. As the distortion effects values is lowered, the nausea effect is increasingly replaced by a green [[screen effect]] around the edges of the screen. At lower values the warp and wobble effect is lesser and the green overlay effect is greater, and vice versa. At 100%, the green overlay is entirely disabled, and at "Off" (0%), the distortion is entirely disabled. The effect can be removed by drinking [[Milk Bucket|milk]].

entities.blurb: Night Vision is a status effect that enhances the player's ability to see in darkness and underwater.
entities.name: Night Vision

sections.behaviour: Night Vision greatly increases the brightness, so the player can easily see in a light level of 0. However, it is not as bright as a [[light]] level of 15 (e.g. with the "Moody" brightness setting, it is similar to block light level 12–13 and no sky light in the Overworld within the "Bright" brightness setting), and unlike block lighting it is not tinted. As such, the player can distinguish between light levels. With [[Vibrant Visuals]], the game specifically enhances the gamma of ambient light (noticable without other light sources) and sky light during nighttime. If the player has Night Vision without Vibrant Visuals, the [[fog]]'s color in gets brightened depending on the [[biome]]. It turns bright red in [[Nether wastes]] and [[crimson forest]], magenta in [[warped forest]], bright cyan in [[soul sand valley]], gray-white in [[basalt deltas]], and pale purple in [[the End]]. In [[Java Edition 20w14∞]], in certain dimensions with unique lighting, the player can see the color spectrum that is not parts of the vanilla lighting system (e.g. vivid shades of green, blue, etc.) easily as the effect is not as fully bright, even with the "Bright" brightness setting (in other cases, in some dimensions (such as Easter egg dimensions like ant) already have the full brightness at any light levels (including light level 0), so the Night Vision effect is indifferent from the player without the effect in the dimensions). However, the extreme darkest saturated color that can be seen in the uniquely generated dimension with this status effect is blue within the relative luminance value of exactly 0.0722 (as in an Easter egg dimension called blue).

entities.blurb: Raid Omen is a variant of the Bad Omen status effect that causes raids to start when the player is in vicinity of a village.
entities.name: Raid Omen

sections.behaviour: When Raid Omen expires, a [[raid]] begins. The center is the position where the player triggered the start of a raid after the Raid Omen expiration. Raid Omen's potency alters the raid composition and rewards. See [[Raid]] for details. Raid Omen is a [[status effect]] and can be removed through all conventional methods, such as drinking [[milk]] or dying. The player can still receive the Raid Omen effect in Peaceful difficulty via commands (Bad Omen will not transform into Raid Omen in Peaceful), but no raid will trigger when it expires.

This means any equipped armor pieces still lose the usual amount of durability, even at level 5+ where the potion effect grants complete immunity to most sources.

entities.blurb: Saturation is a status effect that restores hunger and saturation.‌[JE  only]
entities.name: Saturation

sections.behaviour: The Saturation effect instantly replenishes 1 × level and 2 × level points of saturation. If the effect lasts longer than one tick, the player continues gaining 1 hunger point and 2 saturation points on each tick, with 20 ticks (1 second) completely replenishing the player's hunger bar and saturation. Negative levels decrease [[hunger]] and saturation. Saturation had its duration set in game ticks (instead of seconds) with the /effect command.

entities.blurb: Slow Falling is a status effect that causes midair entities to more gradually descend downward and avoid fall damage, but prevents critical hits and smash attacks.
entities.name: Slow Falling

sections.behaviour: The affected entity falls at a much slower rate than normal, with a [[Gravity|terminal velocity]] of 9.8 m/s, and is unable to take fall damage when falling. However, the entity still takes damage from using an ender pearl. In addition, the entity cannot turn farmland into dirt by jumping on it. Higher levels do not decrease fall speed further. Effects on certain activities: Sprinting with the Slow Falling effect allows the [[player]] to jump across a gap of 5 blocks (6 blocks with enough momentum), compared to 4 (5 blocks with enough momentum) blocks normally. Unboosted [[elytra]] flight is twice as efficient, but four times slower. Boosts work at normal speed, but the momentum gained doesn't last as long. The player cannot land a critical hit while having this effect. The player cannot perform a smash attack with the [[mace]] while having this effect.

entities.blurb: Slowness is a status effect that causes entities to move slower, contrary to Speed.
entities.name: Slowness

sections.behaviour: Slowness reduces movement speed. Movement includes [[walking]], [[sprinting]], [[sneaking]], [[crawling]], and [[swimming]]. If a player or mob is [[riding]] another mob, Slowness only reduces the speed of the ridden mob if that mob has the effect. The speed of the rider does not matter. Slowness decreases movement speed by 15% × level and contracts the player's field of view accordingly. [[Jumping]], [[Entity#Motion of entities|falling]], [[climbing]], [[flying]], and any motion that is not caused directly by the [[player]] or [[mob]] with Slowness, are not affected by Slowness. i.e. the player or mob will jump / fall / etc. at the same speed as normal.

entities.blurb: Trial Omen is a variant of the Bad Omen effect, which is granted when a non-ominous trial spawner enters the line of sight of a player with Bad Omen. Trial Omen causes nearby trial spawners to become ominous trial spawners, which cause ominous trials to start.
entities.name: Trial Omen

sections.behaviour: When a player receives the Trial Omen effect, they start an [[ominous trial]], and blue flames appear on their body. This is purely visual and does not damage the player. Any trial spawner within 15 blocks of a player with Trial Omen and with a line of sight to the player immediately becomes ominous and joins the ominous trial. This transformation does not affect the duration of the status effect, and does not cause it to stop. This effect is required to unlock an [[Ominous Vault]]. Trial Omen is a [[status effect]] and can be removed through all conventional methods, such as drinking [[milk]], using a [[totem of undying]], or [[dying]].

entities.blurb: Bad Luck is a status effect found exclusively in Java Edition and Legacy Console Edition that decreases the chance of the player getting high-quality loot, contrary to Luck.
entities.name: Bad Luck

sections.behaviour: Bad Luck subtracts the effects level from the [[Attribute#Luck|luck attribute]], which affects the results of [[loot table]]s, with a lower attribute value decreasing the amount and quality of results. The number of rolls is increased by the [[Loot table#Pool|pools]] "bonus rolls"-value times this attributes value, rounded down, and the weight of each [[Loot table#Entry|entry]] is increased by its quality times this attributes value, also rounded down. Quality is currently only used by [[fishing]].

entities.blurb: Weakness is an effect that decreases melee attack damage. It is required to cure zombie villagers.

sections.behaviour: Melee damage inflicted by the affected entity is reduced by 4 × level. Negative levels increase melee [[damage]] dealt. Attacks that deal 0 or less due to Weakness will fail to connect entirely, making them do no [[Knockback (mechanic)|knockback]]. However, by use of damage-increasing enchantments such as [[Sharpness]], [[Smite]], [[Bane of Arthropods]], or [[Impaling]], attacks will always connect. This effect is also used to cure [[zombie villager]]s, preceding the [[golden apple]]. The effect can be removed by drinking [[milk]].

entities.blurb: Weaving is a status effect that lessens the movement speed decrease from being in a cobweb, as well as causing cobwebs to be placed upon death.
entities.name: Weaving

sections.behaviour: Entities with Weaving are less affected by the usual speed decrease that entities suffer from while moving through [[cobweb]]s, allowing them to walk through them at 50% speed instead of 25%. Weaving also causes any [[entities]] that have the effect to spawn cobwebs in an area around the entity upon its death, making it the only [[renewable]] source of cobwebs. 2–3 cobwebs can spawn in a 3×3×3 cube centered on the affected entity. The cobwebs can spawn only on top of existing blocks. These existing blocks must have a full face on the top side, meaning that cobwebs cannot spawn on top of other cobwebs. Mobs affected by Weaving emit web-like [[particles]]. When the [[game rule]] mobGriefing is set to false, entities excluding the player do not generate cobwebs upon death.

entities.blurb: Wind Charged is a status effect that causes an entity to release a burst of wind upon short delay after death.
entities.name: Wind Charged

sections.behaviour: Wind Charged causes any [[entities]] that have the effect to emit a burst of wind, similar to that caused by a thrown [[wind charge]], at the center of the entity's [[hitbox]] upon its death. Mobs affected by Wind Charged emit wind-like [[particles]].
